A.explanation: Horizontal motion has uniform velocity, so horizontal displacement against time should be a straight line, not a curve with decreasing gradient.

B.explanation: Vertical motion starts from rest with uniform acceleration, so the gradient must increase from zero, not decrease as shown.

C.explanation: Horizontal motion has zero acceleration, so horizontal displacement cannot have an increasing gradient of the form $s \propto t^2$.

D.explanation: Vertical displacement from rest with uniform acceleration follows $s = \tfrac{1}{2}at^2$, giving zero initial gradient and increasing gradient, as shown.

hints: Look at the axis labels: two options plot horizontal displacement and two plot vertical displacement, so decide which component can give a curved displacement-time graph.
Recall that the gradient of a displacement-time graph equals velocity, so uniform velocity means constant gradient and uniform acceleration from rest means gradient starting at zero and increasing.
Use $s_x = vt$ for the horizontal part and $s_y = \tfrac{1}{2}at^2$ for the vertical part from rest to decide which curved shape is possible.
walkthrough: Identify the two separate motions: horizontal velocity $v$ is uniform, while vertical motion starts from $u = 0$ with uniform acceleration $a$.
Recall the rule for displacement-time graphs: gradient equals velocity. Constant velocity gives a straight line, increasing velocity gives a curve with increasing gradient.
For the horizontal direction, $s_x = vt$, so the $s_x$-time graph must be a straight line through the origin. Neither curved horizontal graph can be correct.
For the vertical direction, $s_y = ut + \tfrac{1}{2}at^2 = \tfrac{1}{2}at^2$ since $u = 0$. This is a parabola starting with zero gradient and getting steeper as velocity $v_y = at$ grows.
A curve with decreasing gradient would mean decreasing velocity, which contradicts uniform vertical acceleration from rest.
Only the vertical displacement graph with zero initial gradient and increasing gradient matches $s_y \propto t^2$. This is option D.
